old_findings.note: The params offset is still never named and now sits on 505 lines (1761 times), was 452 (1485): values that were held in variables are inlined, see the regression.

regressions.decompiled: address(stor10[Mask(200, 56, sha3(cd[_param1 + Mask(27, 5, uint32(cd[_param1 + 100]) + 31) + cd[32 * idx + ...] + 196], ... 6 words ...))].field_0) = ...  (912-1068 chars per line)
regressions.old: _900 = sha3(...6 words...) / if not stor10[Mask(200, 56, _900)].field_1024: / address(stor10[Mask(200, 56, _900)].field_0) = ...  (60-216 chars)
regressions.source: CLPositionManager._mint: poolKeys[poolId] = poolKey when not yet stored (poolId = keccak256(abi.encode(poolKey)))
regressions.issue: Expressions the old text held in a variable (the poolId hash _900) are now inlined at every use, so 7 poolKeys lines grow fivefold; lines over 800 chars 36 -> 47 in this function, 24 -> 28 in unknowneb80d35e, lines over 240 chars 228 -> 253.
regressions.rule: Bind a pure expression used more than once, or longer than a threshold, to a named variable at its first evaluation, whatever the source of its operands (calldata, memory, storage).

regressions.decompiled: return memory / from mem[64] / len v - mem[64]
regressions.old: return mem[mem[64]], mem[128], mem[mem[64] + 64 len v - mem[64] - 64]
regressions.issue: The return lost its head words: the old text showed the offset word and the count mem[128]; the new one is a bare memory range (same bytes).
regressions.rule: When a returned memory range starts with words written in the same block (mem[P] = 32, mem[P + 32] = n), print those words as values before the rest of the range.

regressions.function: unknowneb80d35e(bytes,bytes[]) and unknownab6291fe(bytes): the mint-liquidity settle path
regressions.source: SafeCast/DeltaResolver revert with a selector and an address argument
regressions.issue: The address is now traced to its storage origin (better), but the error is printed as a 16-byte and a 20-byte piece instead of the selector and an address word, as the 3 other 0x4c085bf1 reverts of the function still are.
regressions.rule: Revert data of the form 4-byte constant then a 32-byte word whose top 12 bytes are zero print as 'selector, address(x)', whatever expression x is.

regressions.source: Notifier: if (gasleft() < unsubscribeGasLimit) revert ...; notifyUnsubscribe{gas: unsubscribeGasLimit}
regressions.issue: With the immutable limit read as 0 the comparison folds away, and the GAS read is now printed as an unused variable.
regressions.rule: Drop an assignment whose value is never used when its expression has no effect (a GAS read included); keeping each GAS read as its own value only matters for the reads that are used.

new_findings.decompiled: mem[mem[64]] = mem[512] / return Bytes(16, 0), mem[mem[64] + 16 len 16]
new_findings.issue: Decoded now (was 'return memory'), but the value is read back through the word just stored instead of being shown as the low 16 bytes of the returned word.
new_findings.rule: A read of memory just written in the same block (mem[P + 16 len 16] after mem[P] = X) is Mask(128, 0, X): print return uint128(X).

improvements: P2 19 -> 2 and P6 gone: 25 'call 0x0.mem[_V len 4]' calls are named (take, settle, sync, withdraw, deposit, balanceOf, unknowna54b2831...), results read as ext_call.return_data[0], 48 'revert with memory' forwards are one line, 'NOT_MINTED' / 'ALREADY_MINTED' / 'INVALID_RECIPIENT' and 0x90bfb865 reverts resolved; permit/permitBatch return '' instead of 32, 0; getPositionLiquidity returns a value; the transient slot prints with 64 digits. Both handler functions shrank by ~300 lines.
notes: Diff 5970 lines: the two handler functions (unknowneb80d35e, unknownab6291fe, mirror-image hunks) reviewed by structure: call, require, revert, return and log counts equal old vs new (63 calls, 88/84 requires, 224/226 reverts, 8 logs); read the changed lines of unknowneb80d35e with the free-memory-pointer patterns filtered out, and the settle path (sync, transferFrom/transfer + settle, settle with value). tokenURI is neutral (same bytes, one slice instead of length/data/padding; a dead padding write dropped).
summary: Calls in the action handlers are now named and their results and reverts resolved, but four readability regressions: inlined former variables make lockAcquired's lines longer (finding 1 worse), multicall's return is a bare memory range, two custom-error reverts print as byte pieces, and dead GAS reads show as unused variables.
